newsitem.title: USA: Intel comfortable with 60 pct year margin.
newsitem.headline: Intel comfortable with 60 pct year margin.

text.p: Intel Corp Chief Financial Officer Andy Bryant said Tuesday he was "relatively comfortable" with gross profit margins of 60 percent, plus or minus a few points, for 1997.
Last Friday Intel said it expected second-quarter results to be below expectations and that gross margins would decline from the first quarter's 64 percent.

The company also said Friday that gross margins for the rest of the year would be around 60 percent, plus or minus a few points, and that first quarter results and current expectations pointed toward the mid- to high-end of that range.
"I am still relatively comfortable with that," Bryant said.
Earlier today Intel Chairman Andrew Grove said the company was engaged in one of its most rapid product transitions ever as it moves to the Pentium II processor from its classic Pentium.
Bryant and other Intel officials, speaking at an analysts' meeting, said that by mid-1998 the Pentium II will be half of Intel's manufacturing output.
Sales of the Pentium classic processor will continue to decline, as they did from the 1996 fourth quarter to the first quarter of this year, they said.
"We said first-quarter shipments of the older Pentium declined sequentially from the fourth quarter," said Paul Otellini, Intel executive vice president. "We expect that to continue."
Otellini said he is comfortable with current forecasts by Dataquest Inc that the worldwide PC market will grow at a compound annual rate of 17 percent through the year 2000.
He said it is too early to tell if the decline in Intel's European chip sales will translate into an entire PC sector decline.
"We are seeing a more than seasonal decline in our European chip sales," Otellini said. "It's too soon to tell whether that will translate into a PC change."
